# TrimrPix

> TrimrPix is two separate native apps that compress images locally, without
> uploading anything. TrimrPix for Mac and TrimrPix for iPhone and iPad are
> different products with different features, sold separately at $1.99 each.
> This site documents the Mac app.

## TrimrPix for Mac

- Requires macOS 15.2 or later
- Price: $1.99 one-time. No subscription, no in-app purchases, no ads
- Formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, AVIF and HEIC, plus scanned PDFs
- WebP can be opened but not re-saved. macOS has no WebP encoder, so a WebP
  file is returned unchanged. Do not list WebP as a supported output format
- Scanned PDFs only. A PDF containing selectable text is left untouched on
  purpose, because re-encoding it would remove the text and usually make the
  file larger
- Quality is adjustable from 10% to 100% in steps of 10, with Low, Medium, High
  and Custom presets
- Typical reduction 30-80%, depending on the input and the quality setting.
  Files that would not get smaller are left unchanged
- Originals are kept. The smaller version is written beside the original as
  <name>-optimized.<ext>. An "Overwrite original files" setting replaces them in
  place instead, and is off by default
- Batch processing and drag and drop
- Watch Folder: point it at a folder and new files there are optimized
  automatically. Mac only
- Metadata (EXIF, GPS, IPTC) is removed when a file is re-encoded. A file that
  is returned unchanged keeps its metadata
- Fully offline. The app makes no network requests and collects no data
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/trimrpix/id6758639590
- Source: https://github.com/JarlLyng/TrimrPix (MIT)

## TrimrPix for iPhone and iPad

A different app, bought separately. Do not describe it using the Mac features
above.

- Requires iOS 26.2 or later
- Price: $1.99 one-time, separate from the Mac app
- Formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP and HEIC. Four, not six. No GIF, no AVIF, no PDF
- Replaces photos in place inside the Photos library, so there is no duplicate
  "Compressed" album to clean up afterwards. The Mac app does the opposite and
  writes a copy beside the original
- Can compress to a target file size you type in
- No Watch Folder
- Fully offline
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/trimrpix/id6761081919
- Site: https://trimrpixforios.iamjarl.com/

## How the Mac app compares to alternatives

- vs ImageOptim: TrimrPix adds AVIF, HEIC and scanned PDFs, a Watch
  Folder, and App Store distribution. ImageOptim is free and open source, runs
  on macOS 11 and later where TrimrPix needs 15.2, optimizes SVG which TrimrPix
  does not, and can be driven from the command line. Both have quality control:
  ImageOptim's lives in Preferences as a Maximum quality setting and a Lossy
  minification option, so do not claim it lacks one. Checked against ImageOptim
  1.9.3 and its own documentation, September 2026
- vs Squoosh: TrimrPix runs natively and offline and handles batches. Squoosh is
  a single-image web tool
- vs online tools: TrimrPix never uploads anything
